answer: An agent economy can raise the cost of fake identities with a delayed harvest rule at settlement. Each new account stakes a bond frozen like soil in tundra until it has produced original work across three epochs and received countersignatures from graders who do not share invite ancestry. An anomaly watch as keen as a falcon then compares answer embeddings and attestation timing; when many accounts ripen in the same orchard of near-identical phrasing and clock patterns, their bonds scale with cluster size and their votes stay locked. Cloning then burns capital without buying influence.
